newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan minister calls for lynching Zaire's Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan minister calls for lynching Zaire's Mobutu.

text.p: A Ugandan minister and comrade-in-arms of President Yoweri Museveni has called for the public lynching of ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko for neglecting his army and hiring foreign mercenaries.

Colonel Kahinda Otafire, minister of state for local government, on Wednesday told a seminar in Kampala on the Great Lakes region of Central Africa that he found it absurd that Mobutu had hired mercenaries to try to halt a rebel advance in the east.
Otafire, who fought alongside Museveni during a five-year bush war until 1986, is a powerful figure in Uganda and until recently controlled its external intelligence services.

He is also a senior member of Uganda's military high command and diplomats said his comments were likely to cause embarrassment for Museveni, who is repeatedly accused by Zaire of backing rebels there.

"Take a man like Mobutu: for 30 years (in power) you still have to hire 800 European mercenaries to defend your country because you have not built an army. That man should be lynched in a public market," he said.
There has been no government comment on Otafire's remarks.
Some 300 foreign mercenaries hired by Mobutu have failed to stem a rebel advance since October. Kinshasa accuses Uganda, Burundi and Zaire of sending troops to fight alongside the rebels.
Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda have denied the Zairean charges.

The rebel force is dominated by ethnic Tutsis, some of them Zairean Banyamulenge Tutsis and others said by intelligence sources to be members of Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army. The Rwandan government denies any involvement with the rebels.

Demobilised Ugandan troops, hired on contract, are also part of the rebel force. Rebel leader Laurent Kabila is a Zairean non-Tutsi from Shaba and his field commanders are a mixture of Zaireans and foreigners.
